title: Blue Notebook Review - Superbowl Edition
description:
Just in time for the big game—here’s this week’s Blue Notebook Review ⚡

Traffic enforcement is only part of the story. Stay through the full video to hear from four Neighborhood Resource Officers covering crime suppression, community outreach, and ongoing efforts focused on homelessness in Santa Monica.

A few minutes. A full citywide snapshot.

For a more detailed report, visit https://www.santamonica.gov/blog/the-blue-notebook-a-weekly-smpd-recap-january-18-24-2025
transcript_text: The best actor award goes to Sergeant Rick for his role in The Blue Notebook. >> Oh man, I can't believe I won best actor for my role in the Blue Notebook. I want to thank you, Walter Van, for believing the intro in last week's video was real. Clearly, my acting was on point. But rest assured, there was no makeup on the brush. Truth be told, the coffee was actually pretty cold. Took several takes for me to stop laughing and smiling when I was trying to be mad at our cadet. But Walter and Christopher, fear not. We also sent officers down to Ocean Washington to patrol Palisades Park. You see, I have a saying that I used for years. Why or when you can ant? What that means in this context is we can still police the city of Santa Monica and give you weekly updates on the work we've done. With all that aside, my name is Sergeant Rick with the San Police Department and this is your blue notebook review. And remember, this is an overview. This isn't all the things that we've done last week. If you want that information, we do have it. Stop by our website. I'll put the link below and you can visit and see all every call for service and every arrest that we've made. Okay, let's go out in the field and let's hear from let's start with Enro Tago who's going to cover homelessness. Taga, it's all yours. >> Thanks, Ar. Hello everybody. I'm here to speak to you about homelessness. The Santa Monica Police Department continued its balanced approach of outreach, enforcement, and service-based engagement. Our homeless lays on program officers or better known as our help team conducted 203 selfinitiated contacts. So, what self initiated means is our officers are actively patrolling the city. They're seeing violations and they're addressing on the spot versus when you, the community, call us. They also conducted numerous area focused patrols, whether that be in a vehicle or on foot and address numerous encampments throughout the city. A instant of notice, our officers contacted a subject who was in violation of our doorway ordinance, which states, "You may not sit or lie in front of the doorway between the hours of 11 pm and 7 a.m." After contacting the subject, officers learned that he had a felony Nobel warrant, and he was ultimately transported to the Santa Monica jail. The Santa Monica Police Department also assisted with the annual homeless count where we deployed officers in our drone system to assist with the counting. I just want to speak to you, the community, real quick about our 311 system. If there is furniture in your alley, if there's a mattress, if there's discarded trash, please utilize the 311 system. If you need officers out there right away, if there's an encampment, if there's a violation where somebody may be harmed, please call the non-emergency number right here below. Uh, that's all I have here in Pal Park. Back to you in the studio, Sarge. >> Hey, thanks, Tago. Let's hear from Enro Partardo, who has a traffic update for us. Izzy, what do you got? >> Thanks, Sarge. Hello, everyone. I'm officer Partardau, your B2 neighborhood resource officer. Quick traffic update. Traffic safety stayed a priority this week with officers out citywide doing targeted enforcement and education. Motor officers focused on school zones, downtown Santa Monica, and posted sign compliance because signs aren't suggestions, even when you're in a hurry. We also conducted a DUI saturation patrol that resulted in multiple stops and one drugrelated arrest. Impaired driving is dangerous and completely preventable. Officers investigated a vehicle pedestrian collision near a local elementary school involving an autonomous vehicle. No injuries thankfully and a reminder that people always come first. Slow down, look up, and enjoy Super Bowl weekend. Back to you in the studio, Sarge. >> Thanks, Izzy. And I have no doubt Officer Hollowell is going to bring the energy into our next segment where he's talking about crime. Hollowwell, you there? >> Thanks, Sarge. Steven Hollowwell, your neighborhood resource officer here in the field for beat number one. Crime suppression for this operational period was outstanding. Downtown services, the crime impact team K9, as well as patrol officers were able to respond to 2,649 calls for service as well as 16 arrests. Bing bong. That's amazing. I want to tell you about two particular incidents that officers were able to respond to. The downtown service unit was conducting crime suppression near the pier. Did you know that is it is illegal to trespass under the pier due to the tideline can be a little dangerous? While officers from the DSU were conducting this crime suppression, they came upon two people who were under the pier who had narcotics paraphernalia adjacent to their person. They conducted their stop and did a patown search incident to arrest for the violation and discovered that one person had more narcotics on their person as well as in possession of a firearm. Both were taken to jail fourth with good job DSU. The second incident is patrol officers responded to a radio call for service for a trespasser at the location. Security saw on camera that this individual had a gun. Officers responded with the quickness and were able to identify that he indeed did have a gun because they heard one shot being fired. Field deployed drone went up in the air to help provide containment, which was excellent. Los Angeles Police Department airship responded to provide an overview of the location to make sure all the holes were covered with the responding patrol officers. Also, the crime impact team was able to locate our rescue vehicle and bring it to scene to make sure that we had maximum coverage to responding to this individual with maximum safety for the officers. The suspect was taken into custody for firing in the air and trespassing at the location without incident. Great job team. That's the way we should do it. Hey Sarge, back to you in the studio. Thanks Hollowell. Bing bong. You never disappoint with your enthusiasm. And now to officer to talk about our community engagement efforts. And it it looks like he's enjoying a cup of coffee on Montana. Uh Brandon, what do you got? >> Hi Blue No family. Hi, Sarge. I hope you're nice and cool in your air conditioned office. It's a beautiful day out here on Montana. You should come outside, Sergeant. Come play with us sometime. So, during this reporting period, your NRO's met with neighborhood and business owner groups, as well as responded to a variety of emails and voice messages with concerns in the area. The NRO's coordinated with the crime impact team, the help team, as well as our traffic unit to address these issues at hand. Our crime prevention coordinators also conducted security assessments and follow-ups with local businesses. We have a lot of community events coming up. So I truly hope you follow us on social media on all our platforms. Take it back to you Sergeant Studio. Cheers. >> And that my friends concludes this week's Blue Notebook review. We already covered a couple comments in the very beginning, but I want to touch on one from our lifelong real one, JP, who was wondering how many adoptions we had last week. Well, JP, I called the shelter before I hopped in the studio, and we had nine. I think it was two cats and seven dogs. So, for those of you that don't know the importance of that, last year, we made a pack that for every adoption over three, I would donate $20. And then JP said he would match it with $20. Well, let's do the math. 9 - 3 is 6. 6 * 40 is $240. So, we donated $240 to Santa Monica Animal Shelter Foundation. Future Rick, if you could put the receipt up here for us, just so you can see. I'm not kidding. There it is. Oh, and by the time that you see this, it's going to be Super Bowl Sunday. So, I hope whichever team you're rooting for wins. Seahawks. But more importantly, I want you to have a fun and safe Super Bowl. Make sure you plan ahead and get a ride home. Don't Don't risk drinking and driving. It is not worth it. It's not worth it for your safety, the public safety, financially. It's just it's not smart. There's so many apps right there you can use right now to get a ride home. Use them. Call a friend. Have a designated driver. And then how about we close this out with an outtake. I'm sure future Rick is going to go through all the footage and I guarantee there's going to be outtakes. No one's doing this in one take. I'll add that at the end. And remember, be nice. Everybody's going through something. Some just probably don't show it. Until next week. I'll see you then. >> Hey, Sergeant. Thank you. Hello everyone. Officer Partardo. I'm Officer Partardo. How come I can't say that? Okay, one more time. Scrolling. >> Yep. >> Hey, Sarge. Thank you. Hello, everyone. I'm Officer Part because signs aren't signs. Signs. Signs. Signs. Signs. [laughter] My accent.
